subject: chemistry
question_text: What is resonance? Explain it with the ozone molecule as an example.

verification.note: PREDICTED, not asked. This question comes from the enumeration sweep: resonance is an NCERT Chemical Bonding section that the Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.56-61) skips entirely. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. The 2+1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. AI chemistry check 2026-08-25. Added the formal charges of the ozone canonical forms (central O +1, singly bonded terminal O −1) to the s2 `why` — the marked line draws them uncharged, which the formal-charge card of this same chapter computes as +1. The 128 / 121 / 148 pm bond lengths verified correct.

steps.label: Definition
lines: When a single Lewis structure cannot
describe a molecule exactly, the molecule
is described as a resonance hybrid of two
or more Lewis structures, called canonical
The canonical forms differ only in the
positions of electrons, never of atoms.
The hybrid is lower in energy (more
stable) than any single canonical form.
steps.why: The definition has three separately checkable parts: why resonance is needed, what may differ between forms, and that the hybrid is the more stable description.
common_mistakes: Saying the molecule keeps switching between the forms. The real molecule is ONE fixed hybrid; the forms are drawings.
Moving atoms between canonical forms. Only electron positions may differ.
steps.memory_tip: Many drawings, one molecule: electrons move between drawings, atoms never do.
steps.margin_note: Three sentences, three parts of the definition — write all three.

steps.label: Ozone structures
lines: The double bond can be drawn on either
side of the central O atom, so neither
steps.why: Ozone is the standard example because its two forms are mirror placements of one double bond — the simplest possible pair of canonical forms. In a complete Lewis structure each form also carries formal charges: the central O is +1, the singly bonded terminal O is −1 and the doubly bonded terminal O is 0. Board answers accept the plain forms written here, so the marked line keeps them.
common_mistakes: Using a plain arrow → between the forms. The resonance symbol is the double-headed arrow ↔.
Drawing ozone as a ring of three O atoms. It is bent and open.
steps.memory_tip: One double bond, two possible sides — that is the whole pair of forms.
steps.margin_note: The double-headed arrow ↔ is the required notation.

steps.label: The result

lines.text: Both O−O bonds in ozone are identical (128 pm)

lines: This length lies between a single bond
(148 pm) and a double bond (121 pm) —
exactly what a resonance hybrid predicts.
steps.why: The equal, intermediate bond lengths are the experimental evidence: if either drawing were the real molecule, the two bonds would have different lengths.
common_mistakes: Writing one short and one long bond for ozone. Experiment finds the two bonds EQUAL.
steps.memory_tip: 128 sits between 121 and 148 — the hybrid averages its drawings.
steps.margin_note: The three lengths in one line close the argument.
